On Dec 25, 2012, at 5:20 AM, elad bensal <bens...@gmail.com> wrote:

> hi
>
> i want to use the function "ripple" with method="likelihood"
> i read the chapter about the hidden markov .i saw that in the backcross model
> the rqtl library assumes (page 373 in the book) PIE(AB)=PIE(AA)=1/2 i want to ask if i have PIE(AB)=PIE(AA)=p and p doesnt equal to 1/2 how does it affect the LOD in the way that the RQTL calculates it..?

I assume you mean Pr(AB) = p and Pr(AA) = 1-p for some p.

If there is reasonably complete genotype data, results won't be much affected by the presence of such segregation distortion.

> what is the connection between the formula for detection of genotyping error(page 380 in the book) to the LOD score that we calculate by ripple with the method "likelihood"
> the likelihood that i think it should be
> P1^(Kobs)*(1-P1)^(N-Kobs)/(P2^(Kobs)*(1-P2)^(N-Kobs))
> i belive that the RQTL makes this calculation with P2=1/2 am i wrong?

I don't understand what you are after, regarding the connection between the likelihood calculations in ripple() and the genotyping error LOD scores.

R/qtl does all calculations for a backcross assuming equal segregation of alleles, Pr(AA) = Pr(AB) = 1/2 in a backcross.

karl
